To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
people high in the personality dimension of agency (competence) prefer attractive, high-status partners, whereas people high in the dimension of communion (warmth) prefer warm partners.
the Big Two personality dimensions of agency (competence) and communion (warmth) predict Big Three preferences for attractiveness, status, or warmth in a mate.

(a) people high on agency/competence prefer mates with high attractiveness and status and people high on communion/warmth prefer mates with high warmth and (b) this similarity-attracts hypothesis is moderated by agentics' tendency to contrast from and communals' tendency to assimilate with ambient culture.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of why people differ in mate preferences and why these differences vary across cultures.
why people prefer what they prefer in mates.
how personality and culture shape mate preferences.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
people’s mate preferences depend on the Big Two of personality and the Big Three of mate preferences, and that these effects are contingent on the cultural values of the ambient environment.
people prefer similarity in mate characteristics, but this effect is moderated by their own and ambient cultural values.
similarity attracts in mate preferences, but only in the right cultural and personality contexts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

people are more likely to prefer a mate who is similar to them in the Big Two dimensions of personality (agency and warmth), but this similarity-attract effect is moderated by agentic-cultural-contrasts and communal-cultural-assimilarities.
“similarity-attracts” only if one is a communal who is in a culture that does not value warmth.
people are similar in mate preferences to those who are high in the same Big Two personality dimension as they themselves are.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the similarity-attracts principle does not hold for all people in all cultures.
mate choice is a complex process that is best understood when considering how people’s personalities interact with their cultural environments.
mate choice is not just about what people want, but also about what people are like.
